title: Memory That Argues Back
tagline: When a fact gets corrected, the old one has to go.
what: A memory for my AI chats. Before the AI reads a word I type, my setup attaches the notes, settled facts and past work that match it, and the fact list won't quietly hold two answers that disagree.
built: Over 270 notes on how my things work, each tagged so the right one gets pointed at
Short, settled facts attached to the messages they match
A new fact that nearly matches an old one updates it, instead of sitting beside it
A recheck stamp, so a fact nobody has confirmed in a while shows up as stale
credit: Built it on top of Claude Code
starring: Me, and the AI chats I run every day

making.problem: A fresh chat needs the decisions and context from the work before it.

steps.name: Match
steps.says: My message is matched against the keywords on every note and fact.

steps.name: Attach
steps.says: The best few ride along as short pointers, not whole documents.

steps.name: Argue back
steps.says: When a new fact disagrees with an old one, one of them has to go.

moment.what: I correct a fact once and retire the old answer, instead of leaving two versions for the next chat to choose between. A recheck gets its own stamp, so I can tell what we've actually confirmed.
